description: Reviewed rows naming an AWS error as a result other than a failed call (req-aws-collector-outcome). not_taggable rows apply to tag reads only (req-aws-collector-tags): the resource cannot hold tags, so the answer is no tags; they were authored from a live GovCloud probe on 2026-11-06. not_configured: the feature is not set up in this account, so the listing is empty-by-absence and is NOT an authoritative complete-empty observation (it licenses no retirement). unsupported_in_partition: the partition does not offer the service or operation. Rows were authored from the 2026-11-01 GovCloud (us-gov-west-1) wave-0 smoke run. A not_configured row must name its service, error code and operation or entity type: it is never a broad catch. The unsupported_in_partition rows are a stopgap until availability is derived from data; replace them, do not extend them casually.

rows.message_contains: not authorized to do this operation on shared resource
rows.why: The resource is shared into this account from another (a Route 53 Resolver firewall domain list, for example); only its owner may read or set its tags. Observed in GovCloud.
Route 53 Resolver creates auto-defined rules itself and refuses tags on them (RSLVR-00903). Observed in GovCloud.
The SageMaker public hub is owned by AWS (its ARN carries the account 'aws'); the tag API refuses its ARN. Observed in GovCloud.
AWS-defined AppConfig extensions have an ARN with no account id, and the tag API refuses it. Observed in GovCloud.
AwsDataCatalog is the account's built-in Glue-backed catalog; the tag API does not find it as a taggable resource. Observed in GovCloud.
